An orchestra is performing Beethoven's 9th Symphony. There's a part where the bass players have nothing to do for awhile, and they get bored, so they all decide to sneak out of the back row and go across the street to have a few beers at the bar before coming back to finish the performance. They make it out without being discovered, and hurry across the street. They pound a few beers, then one of them points at the time and says they need to get back. But one of them responds that it's okay, they have time for one more beer, because he tied the last few pages of the conductor's score together so it will take him some extra time to get to their part. So they have one more beer, then race across the street and sneak back into the performance.

The bass players are pleased with their successful ploy, and can't help but giggle amongst themselves. Meanwhile, the conductor seems to be having problems with his score, and is fumbling around trying to get to the next page.

This activity is noticed by a couple in the audience. A wife says to her husband, "What's going on here?"

The husband quips, "Can't you see? It's the bottom of the Ninth, the score is tied, and the bassists are loaded."
